data.narrative:
Open Cosmos is a Growth-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Rafel Jorda Siquier, Jordi Barrera Ars, and Aleix Megias Homar. The company has raised $50M to date. The Space & Aerospace sector includes a peer universe of 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers spanning similar segments.

Of three valuation methods tested, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the $50M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage progression, yielding $60M. Peer-Median analysis was not feasible due to insufficient narrow-filter comps in the Space & Aerospace sector—while 14 same-sector peers exist, none satisfied same-stage or adjacent-stage criteria in sufficient numbers. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied because target revenue is not on file; the public sector median P/S multiple of 25.3x across the five public tickers cannot be applied without disclosed revenue data.

The triangulation analysis, constrained by single-method applicability, supports a valuation range of $51M to $69M, with a median of $60M. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable private transaction data at equivalent scale, lack of revenue visibility for revenue multiple calibration, and reliance on a modest stage-progression assumption that may not capture sector-specific risk or capital intensity.
